newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai port aims to expand throughput capacity.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai port aims to expand throughput capacity.

text.p: Shanghai port aims to expand its cargo handling capacity to 220 million tonnes annually by the end of the century and 280 million tonnes by 2010, the China Daily Business Weekly reported on Sunday.
The port handled 163.8 million tonnes of all forms of cargo in 1996, marginally down on the 1995 total of 165.67 million tonnes, according to media reports last week.

The newspaper quoted a city official as saying the plan is to expand the container handling capacity of the port from the present 1.9 million ten-foot-equivalent units (TEUs) to at least 2.5 million TEUs by 2000 and more than six million by 2010.

The city also plans to invest at least 10 billion yuan ($1.2 billion) into dredging the mouth of the Yangtze River over the next decade to make the port, China's largest, accessible to larger container ships.
Shanghai handles one quarter of China's sea cargo and one third of its sea containers.
